title: Frequently Asked Questions
subtitle: Answers to common questions about Sciecola, the Sangia AI Engine, the API, and deployment. If you can't find an answer, contact our support team.

umum.a: An Indonesian research impact analytics platform measuring the contribution of researchers, articles, institutions, and journals using the Sangia Impact Score (Scieco) — a composite of 4 pillars: Academic, Social, Economic, and SDG.

umum.q: What is the Sciecola AI Engine?
umum.a: The Sciecola AI Engine is the AI analytics backend (`api.sangia.org`) that runs heavy computations: SDG classification, impact score, trend analysis, and policy recommendations. Sciecola itself doesn't store data — all persistence is handled by Sciecola. The Engine lives in a separate repo, `sciecola-apis`.

umum.q: Why are there two servers (PHP on port 8000 and Node on port 3000)?
umum.a: In development, PHP serves Twig pages and REST API while Vite serves the React frontend with Hot Module Replacement (HMR). In production only PHP runs — React is built to static files under `public/app/`.

autentikasi.q: Why is login only via ORCID?
autentikasi.a: ORCID is an internationally verified researcher identifier. Signing in with ORCID ensures only real researchers can claim their profile on the platform.

autentikasi.q: What if I don't have an ORCID yet?
autentikasi.a: Register for free at orcid.org. ORCID is the global standard identifier recognized by over 1,000 research organizations.

autentikasi.q: Can admins sign in without ORCID?
autentikasi.a: No. Every account uses ORCID. Admin roles are set in the database (`users.role = 'admin'`) after the first sign-in.

apikey.q: What is the API Key for?
apikey.a: The API Key is used to call the Sangia API Engine directly from other apps or analytics scripts. Key format: `wz_{user_id}_{timestamp}_{hmac16}`.

apikey.q: How long is an API Key valid?
apikey.a: 365 days from creation. After expiry, generate a new key from Dashboard → API Key Management.

apikey.q: What if my API Key leaks?
apikey.a: Click "Revoke API Key" in the Dashboard immediately. The key is blacklisted in the Sangia API Engine and nulled in the database.

apikey.q: Why must SANGIA_SHARED_SECRET match between Sciecola and the APIs?
apikey.a: The Sangia API validates HMAC keys locally without a database roundtrip. For validation to succeed on both sides, the secret must be identical.

scieco.a: Yes. Each computation is inserted (not updated). Score history is kept for trend charts. It can be triggered manually ("Recalculate" button) or automatically via job queue.

scieco.q: Why is my score lower than expected?
scieco.a:
A few possibilities:
• Citation data is not yet updated on Scopus/ORCID (wait 24–48 hours)
• The Social and Economic pillars need manual input that hasn't been filled
• Works outside ORCID are not counted (add them to your ORCID profile)

scieco.q: Can I change the weights of the 4 pillars?
scieco.a: Yes — via Admin Panel → Weight Configuration. Changes are saved in `analysis_weight_configs` and applied to subsequent computations.

scieco.q: Is Scieco the same as h-index?
scieco.a: No. h-index only measures academic impact (citations). Scieco measures 4 dimensions: academic, social, economic, and SDG contribution. A researcher can have a low h-index but a high Scieco if their work has significant social-economic impact.

sdg.a:
Sangia analyzes titles and abstracts using 4 approaches:
1. SDG keyword matching (weight 30%)
2. Semantic similarity with SDG embeddings (30%)
3. Substantive context analysis (20%)
4. Causal linkage with SDG targets (20%)

sdg.q: What is the maximum number of SDGs attributable to one article?
sdg.a: Default is 7 SDGs. This value can be configured by admins via the `sdg_v5.max_sdgs` weight.

sdg.q: Is SDG v5 different from earlier versions?
sdg.a: Yes. Sangia supports multiple SDG model versions (v4, v5). v5 uses newer embeddings with higher accuracy on Indonesian-language text.

database.a:
• `database_schema_full.sql` — full schema from scratch
• `database_migration_v2.sql` — additional tables for the Sangia API v2 integration (cache, weight configs, API logs). Run it after schema_full.

database.q: Is it safe to run `database_migration_v2.sql` repeatedly?
database.a: Yes. All statements use `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` and `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, so re-runs are safe.

frontend.q: Why Vite instead of Create React App (CRA)?
frontend.a: Vite is much faster: HMR (hot reload) is nearly instant vs 10–30 seconds in CRA. Production builds are also smaller thanks to Rollup with aggressive tree-shaking.

An object injected by PHP into the page before React loads, containing:
• apiUrl: "/api/v1" — API backend URL
• currentUser: { id, full_name } — currently signed-in user
• csrfToken: "abc123..." — CSRF token for POST requests
• appPath: "/app" — React Router base path

React reads this object via `window.__SANGIA_INIT__` at startup.

This is a Single Page Application — routing happens client-side. On a hard refresh, the browser requests `/app/researchers/123` from PHP. The route config `/app/{path:.+}` (catch-all with regex `.+`) makes PHP always return the React shell so React Router can handle navigation.

frontend.q: How do I change the interface language?
frontend.a:
By default the language is detected from the browser. To force it:

```js
import i18n from './i18n';
i18n.changeLanguage('en'); // or 'id'
```

The preference is saved in `localStorage`.

crawler.a:
Yes, with caveats:
• Respects `robots.txt` automatically
• Default rate limit of 2 seconds between requests
• Stops automatically when CAPTCHA is detected
• Doesn't store personal data

crawler.q: Why isn't all Google Scholar data available?
crawler.a: Google Scholar has no official public API and actively blocks scraping. SciecolaBot tries best-effort; when CAPTCHA appears the crawl stops and falls back to official APIs (Crossref, Semantic Scholar).

crawler.q: Which data is prioritized for crawling?
crawler.a: Priority order: official APIs (Crossref, Semantic Scholar, OpenCitations) → Sangia API cache → web crawl (Scholar, ResearchGate, Scimago). Official APIs are always more reliable and faster.

deployment.q: How do I deploy to production?
deployment.a:
1. Set `APP_ENV=production` and `APP_DEBUG=false` in `.env`
2. Run `npm run build` → output to `public/app/`
3. Set `TWIG_CACHE=true` for performance
4. Use Nginx/Apache with the config in `docs/INSTALLATION.md`
5. Set `ORCID_SANDBOX=false` for ORCID production
Not required. Redis is used for background job queues (`QUEUE_DRIVER=redis`). If unavailable, set `QUEUE_DRIVER=database` — jobs are stored in a MySQL table.

deployment.q: How do I update the app?
deployment.a:
```bash
git pull origin main
composer install --optimize-autoloader
npm install && npm run build
# Run new migrations if any:
mysql -u root -p sciecola < database_migration_vX.sql
```
